Heavenly Father,
We come before You with heavy hearts, standing in the shadow of war, conflict, and fear. We lift up President Donald Trump, the leaders of Israel, and all those in authority making decisions that affect countless lives around the world. Grant them wisdom that comes from You — a wisdom that seeks peace, values human life, and honors justice above all else.

Lord, we pray for Your Spirit to guide their hearts and minds so that actions taken in fear, pride, or anger would be replaced with patience, courage to seek peace, and resolve to protect the innocent. Dear President Donald Trump,

This is not just a letter.
This is a cry from the heart of a nation.

Inside Iran, millions of civilians are living under heavy psychological pressure, fear, isolation, and economic hardship. Communication disruptions and restrictions have made many people feel cut off from the world. Families feel anxious every day. Parents fear for their children’s safety. Young people feel their future fading.

We are exhausted.

We are not asking for war.
We are not asking for conflict.

We are asking for humanity.

The Iranian people are not the same as the system that governs them. Many of us feel trapped in circumstances we did not choose. We want the same simple things other nations want: safety, dignity, opportunity, and the freedom to build our country in peace.

President Trump, please listen to the voices of innocent Iranian civilians. When a nation quietly cries for help, history remembers who chose to listen.

Do not let our silence become permanent.

We are human beings.
We deserve life without fear.
We deserve hope.

Respectfully,
An Iranian Citizen

The Shah will return to his country. All Iranians stand behind him. Long live the Shah — King Reza Pahlavi. Javid Shah.”

comment.base:
Northern Kingdom of Israel (10 tribes)

1. Ahab

Tribe: Ephraim through Jeroboam’s line
Wife: Jezebel
• Promoted worship of Baal on a national level
• Built a temple for Baal in Samaria
• Opposed by the prophet Elijah

God’s response in the text:
• A severe drought
• Fire from heaven on Mount Carmel
• Judgment pronounced on Ahab’s house

Ahab is basically the poster king for Baal corruption in Israel.

⸻

2. Jeroboam I
• Didn’t push Baal directly
• But created golden calves at Bethel and Dan
• Led Israel into idolatry that opened the door for later Baal worship

His phrase in Scripture becomes almost a refrain: “He caused Israel to sin.”

⸻

Southern Kingdom of Judah (tribes of Judah & Benjamin)

3. Solomon

Yes, that Solomon.
• Built high places for foreign gods because of his wives
• Included Molech
• Also for Ashtoreth and Chemosh

God’s response:
The kingdom was torn in two after his death.

⸻

4. Manasseh

One of the darkest chapters.
• Practiced sorcery
• Set up idols in the Temple
• Caused children to pass through fire, associated with Molech worship

God’s response:
Declared coming destruction on Jerusalem. Judah would eventually fall to Babylon.

⸻

5. Ahaz
• Burned his son as an offering
• Followed detestable practices of surrounding nations

Judah suffered invasions during his reign.👹✡️🚫

comment.base: ​A Trail of Destabilization: From Baghdad to Benghazi​The potential for conflict in Iran is not an isolated threat; it is merely the latest chapter in a long history of intervention-led displacement. To understand why millions seek refuge in the West, one must look at the "shatter zone" created by previous decades of conflict:​Iraq & Libya: Direct military interventions in these nations dismantled existing state structures, leading to years of power vacuums, civil war, and the rise of extremist groups.​Syria & Yemen: Prolonged proxy wars, often fueled by external weapons and funding, have turned these nations into the sites of the world's worst humanitarian crises.​Sudan & Nigeria: Internal strife, often exacerbated by global economic pressures and competition for resources, has forced millions from their ancestral lands.​Pakistan: Decades of being caught in the crossfire of regional "wars on terror" have led to massive internal and external displacement.​The Cumulative Effect​When we list these countries together, a clear map of migration emerges. These aren't just names on a map; they represent a continuous belt of instability. Each time a "major combat operation" is launched or a local government is undermined, the "means to peace" for the local population are spoiled.​The West, having played a role in the destabilization of these regions—through direct war, arms sales, or political maneuvering—eventually becomes the destination for those with nowhere else to go.​The Reality: Migration is the "echo" of a bomb dropped years prior. You cannot have decades of "interventionist" foreign policy without expecting the human displacement that inevitably follows.​Making the Connection​By looking at Libya, Syria, Yemen, Iraq, Pakistan, Nigeria, and Sudan, it becomes clear that the "Migrant Crisis" is actually a "Consequence Crisis." The West is essentially receiving the human results of its own global footprint.
